unit.title: Angles and Constructions
unit.blurb: Corresponding and alternate angles on parallel lines, the exterior angle of a triangle, and ruler-and-compasses constructions.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Recognise corresponding, alternate and vertically opposite angles on parallel lines and use them to find angles.

O2.t: Use the fact that the exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

O3.t: Construct perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors and triangles with ruler and compasses.

p: When a line crosses two **parallel** lines (marked with arrows), it makes 8 angles.
**Corresponding** angles are equal (an F shape). **Alternate** angles are equal (a Z shape). **Vertically opposite** angles are equal (an X shape).
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so co-interior angles (a C shape) add up to 180°.

lesson.q: On the diagram, a = 70°. Find c, e and f.
steps: on a straight line with e

p: Only angles in matching positions (F, Z or X shapes) are equal. Angles in a C shape add to 180°.

sections.title: The exterior angle of a triangle

p: Extend one side of a triangle. The angle outside the triangle is an **exterior angle**.
**The exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.** It also makes 180° with the interior angle next to it.

p: A **perpendicular bisector** cuts a line in half at right angles. Open the compasses to more than half the line, draw arcs from each end above and below, and join the crossing points.
An **angle bisector** cuts an angle in half. Draw an arc from the vertex across both arms, then equal arcs from those two points; join the vertex to where they cross.
Draw one side with a ruler. Set the compasses to the second length and draw an arc from one end; set them to the third length and draw an arc from the other end. Join the crossing point to both ends.
Leave your construction arcs on the diagram: they show your method.
